title: Cluster sampling of graph colorings with \(\Delta+1\) colors
formal: Are there universal C,c>0 such that WSK dynamics on every finite simple graph with n≥1 vertices and q≥max{2,Δ+1} colors satisfies t_mix(1/4)≤C(nq)^c?
definitions: A state is a proper vertex coloring σ:V→{1,…,q}, meaning adjacent vertices have distinct colors. At each step choose an unordered pair of distinct colors uniformly from all q(q−1)/2 pairs. Form the subgraph induced by vertices having either color. Independently for each connected component, swap its two colors with probability 1/2 and otherwise retain them. The target μ is the uniform distribution over all proper colorings. For a finite-state transition matrix P with target distribution μ, define t_mix(1/4)=min{t∈N: max_x (1/2)∑_y |P^t(x,y)−μ(y)|≤1/4}, with value infinity if no such t exists. One step means the entire stated update, not one vertex recoloring. The graph has no loops or parallel edges and Δ is its maximum vertex degree. Proper q-colorings exist in this range. All initial proper colorings are included, and the polynomial is uniform in both n and q. The explicit requirement q≥2 avoids an undefined color-pair choice on edgeless graphs with q=1; that one-color case has a single state and zero mixing time. The claimed mixing bound includes convergence to the uniform law on the entire state space, not just one communicating class.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated proposition or its negation for the specified model.
context: The 2026 paper obtains strong WSK results on chordal and outerplanar graph classes, rather than all graphs at the Δ+1 threshold.
why: A sharp general-graph guarantee would establish when cluster updates overcome barriers facing single-vertex coloring samplers.

import_provenance.original_statement: Does Wang–Swendsen–Kotecký dynamics mix in polynomial time on every n-vertex graph of maximum degree Δ when q≥Δ+1 colours are available? A step chooses two colours uniformly and independently swaps them on each connected component induced by those colours, with probability 1/2.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: This is an editorial sharp-threshold target for Kotecký’s cluster sampler, not a personal conjecture attributed to him. A July 2026 preprint obtains optimal mixing on chordal and outerplanar graphs, without resolving arbitrary graphs.

sentences: A step resamples every component induced by a chosen pair of colors.
The equilibrium is uniform over all proper colorings.
The available palette has at least one color more than maximum degree.
The desired polynomial must work uniformly as both graph size and palette grow.
Results limited to chordal or outerplanar graphs do not cover this target.
